text.p: The operator of the trans-Alaska oil pipeline said Friday it will reorganize its management structure to adjust to new patterns of North Slope oil production.

The changes, to be effective May 1, will cut the company's four business management units to two, said a spokeswoman for Alyeska Pipeline Service Co., the consortium that operates the system that transports more than one fifth of the nation's domestically produced oil.
A single business unit based in Fairbanks will oversee operations along the 800-mile oil pipeline, said Alyeska spokeswoman Jennifer Ruys.
The second business unit will be in Valdez, overseeing operations at the system's marine terminal and the system of escort tugs for oil tankers in and out of port, she said.
Alyeska's corporate headquarters will remain in Anchorage, Ruys said, but more of the company's workers will be transferred to Fairbanks and Valdez.
Workforce cutbacks, already under way because of planned shutdowns of some of the pipeline's pump stations, will be expanded with the reorganization, she said.
Alyeska currently has 965 employees, she said.
The reorganization will help the pipeline operator respond to North Slope production changes, Alyeska President Bob Malone said in a news release.
Alyeska is owned by seven oil companies with interests on Alaska's North Slope.
Major owners are British Petroleum, Atlantic Richfield and Exxon. Mobil, Unocal, Phillips Petroleum and Amerada Hess own minor shares.
